citations.text: OpenEvo comparison of Pillow (2012), Barzilai and Chinn (2018, 2024) and Hanisch and Eirdosh (2023), 2026-11-18. A shared field concept proposed by the comparison; no source defines it.
Pillow, B. H. (2012). Children's discovery of the active mind: Phenomenological awareness, social experience, and knowledge about cognition. Springer.
Barzilai, S., & Chinn, C. A. (2018). On the goals of epistemic education: Promoting apt epistemic performance. Journal of the Learning Sciences, 27(3), 353-389.
Hanisch, S., & Eirdosh, D. (2023). Behavioral science and education for sustainable development: Towards metacognitive competency. Sustainability, 15(9), 7413.

en.general: Teachers talking about, modeling and reflecting on thinking, both as a way to build learners' metacognitive knowledge and as their own epistemic or metacognitive performance. Pillow reports a list of teacher practices taken from Schraw's work. Barzilai and Chinn (2024) review other researchers' work on a reflection cycle for teachers and on teachers' own epistemic performance. The Hanisch and Eirdosh paper reports a teacher education module in development, with preliminary evidence cited from work in review.

examples: A teacher explains why thinking about thinking helps and models her own thinking aloud.
Teachers name the epistemic aims of a lesson and reflect on whether practice reached them.

labels.en: Teachers as Models and Learners of Thinking

nonExamples: A lesson delivered with no talk about thinking.
